items.title: Vince Lateano interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 8, 2002
items.q: I got more into Blakey and Max and Philly Joe and Roy Haynes and those guys.

ctx.x: He had a lot of style, didn’t he?

Oh he was just — I mean he had it all, you know, for a big band. I mean he was just so dynamic. Here this band is just quietly steaming along and all of a sudden it explodes right in front of your eyes. It would just like — when you’re a kid especially it would just throw you back. And then he was just so much fun to watch. And I don’t play anything like that. But he knocked me out. And of course then later on Shelly Manne and Mel Lewis and Woodyard, who I loved, Sam Woodyard. You know, that kind of thing. And…
Right. What’s it like trying to absorb the Latin end of things? Because I know you’ve worked with Cal Tjader.
